newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares open higher, Peugeot falls on profit.
newsitem.headline: French shares open higher, Peugeot falls on profit.

text.p: French shares opened higher on Thursday in the wake of an overnight gain on Wall Street and were also slightly helped by the German IFO figures, dealers said.
The CAC-40 index was up 14.99 points, or 0.57 percent, at 2635.96 and the April future added 15.5 to 2,633.5. Dealers said there could be a retreat to 2,625 after a rise to 2,644.
Peugeot was down 3.44 percent at 617 francs after it disappointed with a 57 percent profit drop to 734 million francs and a decision to cut its dividend.
U.S. international trade for February and initial jobless claims due at 1230 GMT.
Total, up 3.05 percent at 479.50, and Elf, up 1.44 percent at 563, both said they were considering a share buy-back. The two oil stocks were the top volume shares.

Reinsurer SCOR, up 0.87 percent at 232, said it expected a capital gain of 165 million francs on the sale of shares in Coflexip, down 0.56 percent at 322.10, executed on Tuesday after market close by CDC Bourse.
